heroSummary: The Bambu Lab X1C handles Prusament PETG effortlessly out of the box with its direct-drive extruder and hardened steel nozzle, achieving reliable print speeds up to 179 mm/s at a maximum volumetric flow rate of 15 mm³/s. Printing requires no structural hardware modifications, though keeping the top glass vented prevents chamber heat creep during extended jobs.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with liquid glue or glue stick as a release agent
slicerTweaks: Cap the Max Volumetric Speed at 15 mm³/s in the filament settings to eliminate under-extrusion and matte finish banding.
Enable 'Wipe while retracting' set to 2 mm with a Retract Amount Before Wipe of 70% to suppress PETG oozing and stringing.
Set the Pressure Advance (PA) value to 0.034 s (or run dynamic calibration) to maintain uniform extrusion widths through sharp corners.
Lower the Part Cooling Fan to a 20-50% range with the auxiliary fan turned completely off to avoid layer delamination and warping.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Severe fine wispy stringing across travel moves
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Prusament PETG has absorbed ambient moisture, or retraction wiping distance is insufficient.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the filament spool at 65°C for 6 hours in a dedicated dryer and increase Retraction Wipe Distance to 2 mm in OrcaSlicer.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Excessive adhesion causing PEI coating tear-out
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG creates molecular bonds with hot PEI surfaces when printed directly without a barrier interface.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Apply a uniform layer of Bambu Liquid Glue or standard glue stick to act as a release interface before printing.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Weak interlayer bonding and brittle parts
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Auxiliary cooling fan or excessive main part cooling chilling the molten bead prematurely.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Turn off the chamber auxiliary fan (0%) and restrict the main cooling fan to a ceiling of 50% for standard layers.

faq.question: Should I print Prusament PETG with the Bambu Lab X1C door open or closed?
faq.answer: Keep the top glass propped open or front door cracked to prevent chamber temperatures exceeding 40°C, which avoids extruder heat creep and nozzle clogs.

faq.question: Can I use the high-speed 0.02 Pressure Advance default profile for this material?
faq.answer: No, standard Bambu PETG profiles often under-compensate for Prusament's specific viscosity; manual calibration typically yields a higher PA around 0.032 to 0.038.

faq.question: Is the Bambu AMS compatible with Prusament PETG spools?
faq.answer: Yes, standard plastic Prusament spools fit the AMS directly; ensure the spool rim is completely smooth and does not bind against the AMS lid.

faq.question: Why is the top surface finish cloudy or uneven at high speeds?
faq.answer: PETG transitions from glossy to matte when extruded beyond its thermal limit; reduce outer wall and top surface speeds to 80-100 mm/s to retain a uniform glossy finish.
